profile_text.body:
Meta is a public company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, trading on public markets under the ticker META. Its website, llama.com, is oriented toward AI developers and describes the company as offering AI models and tools built around its Llama model family. The site highlights the Meta Model API, which it describes as compatible with existing OpenAI SDK clients, and promotes features including search grounding for live web access and Muse Image, an image generation model priced at $0.01 per image that the site says uses a reasoning approach to plan layout before drawing. A coding-focused model is also described as tuned for long-horizon coding workflows and positioned as competitive with frontier models across coding evaluations. A product called Muse Spark is accessible through Muse Code and the Meta Model API.

The held facts list Llama as Meta's tracked AI product, categorized as an open-weight model family that is often self-hosted. Meta reported revenue of $200,966,000,000 for the period ending 2025-12-31, filed on a 10-K form. Several third-party MCP servers built around Meta's advertising infrastructure appear in the registry, covering campaign management, creative testing, and performance analysis for Facebook and Instagram ads, though these are external integrations rather than Meta's own products.

Meta faces litigation on multiple fronts. Three cases appear in the held facts: Neural AI, LLC v. Meta Platforms, Inc. in the Western District of Texas, Chicken Soup for the Soul, LLC v. Meta Platforms Inc. in the Northern District of California, and Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc., also in the Northern District of California. California is recorded as the jurisdiction with the highest concentration of legal exposure, with 181 cases attributed to that state.
